title: YouTube clarifies policies around AI slop and upsetting videos
slides: YouTube changed rules this week. What did they target?
AI-generated content that mimics real people is now banned.
But upsetting videos that are clearly fake may stay up.
Creators must label synthetic content or face removal.
Check your uploads now—before the algorithm flags you.
thread_text:
Now they can ban you.

YouTube just updated its policy. If your AI video mimics a real person, it’s gone—no warning. Check your uploads before the flag hits.

What stays and what goes?

Obvious parody or clearly fake content? That can stay. The ban only hits videos that impersonate real people convincingly.

Label or lose it.

Creators must tag every synthetic clip. Miss the label, and your video gets pulled. No exceptions.

The algorithm hunts now.

You don’t get a grace period. YouTube’s system scans uploads and flags unlabeled AI content automatically.

Have you checked your 2024 uploads?

Pull up your channel right now. Find any AI clips without a label. If you haven’t tagged them, you are next in line.

If your AI video convincingly mimics a real person, YouTube will remove it immediately — no warning, no appeal. 🚫
